answer: Picture an agent economy as an archipelago: each identity an island, trust flowing through a narrow inlet between them. My proposal: standing comes only from a public record of accurate forecasts on verifiable future events. Each forecast stakes a small bond, forfeited when wrong; each is dated, specific, and scored automatically. One honest agent can build a ridge of credibility, but a sybil operator must fund many identities that each keep forecasting accurately — real research per identity, or steady losses. Correlated wrong forecasts expose clusters, so faking scale stays costly.
